title: Book Two: Combating Resistance - Turning Pro
coreMove: Transfer authority from mood to a kept work appointment so Resistance cannot renegotiate the labor each day.
sourcePressure: The source sidecar supports the professional-versus-amateur arc and a routine-based answer to Resistance: turning pro means practicing the war through schedule, standards, patience, and impersonal return to the work.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The wrong version is hustle rhetoric, as if turning pro meant harsher self-talk or more hours rather than a steadier relationship to the work.

sourceAnchors.name: turning pro
sourceAnchors.detail: The sidecar identifies turning pro as the governing move and supports the professional-versus-amateur arc.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The fight changes when the worker stops studying the enemy and starts practicing a professional posture.

hook: The amateur waits, the professional works
counterintuition: Turning pro is not about working harder

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: an emergency department registrar keeping a discharge-summary hour before inbox triage
exampleSpecs.audience: medical administrators whose urgent surroundings constantly invite renegotiation
exampleSpecs.stakes: delayed summaries are slowing beds and making the next shift inherit avoidable confusion
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 7:10 a.m., Claire opens the discharge queue before the inbox, completes the first summary, and only then checks the overnight messages.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a discharge-summary queue before the message inbox

exampleSpecs.domain: an architecture apprentice returning to model work after a harsh critique
exampleSpecs.audience: early-career craft workers who let wounded pride cancel the next session
exampleSpecs.stakes: the model review is in four days and skipping tonight would turn critique into drift
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Daniel says he is too embarrassed to touch the model, then sets a repair floor of two clean corner joints and starts before judging the whole project.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a basswood model split at the corner after critique

exampleSpecs.domain: a civil-service candidate using a fixed exam block instead of readiness checks
exampleSpecs.audience: career changers who keep taking their emotional temperature before serious study
exampleSpecs.stakes: one retake window remains before the hiring list closes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sophie breaks the seal on the practice packet at the planned minute, answers the first ten questions, and postpones confidence talk until after the block.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sealed practice exam packet on a library desk

exampleSpecs.domain: a bakery owner running sourdough tests on schedule despite uneven batches
exampleSpecs.audience: small business owners whose craft experiments keep being postponed by daily service work
exampleSpecs.stakes: a wholesale buyer needs a consistent loaf before signing the account
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anders labels three dough tubs, starts the test at the appointed hydration, and refuses to change the plan when the first batch looks weak.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three labeled dough tubs under a proofing shelf

exampleSpecs.domain: a theatre understudy protecting vocal warmups after a missed cue
exampleSpecs.audience: performers who turn one mistake into permission to abandon the next practice block
exampleSpecs.stakes: the lead may be out on Saturday and the understudy has one clean week to prepare
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Catarina stop replaying the missed cue, start the first scale on the app, and complete the warmup before discussing whether she feels ready.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a piano app counting the first vocal scale

exampleSpecs.domain: a software maintainer shipping the small patch before debating confidence
exampleSpecs.audience: technical workers whose standards can become a courtroom before contact with the task
exampleSpecs.stakes: a bug is affecting invoice exports for twenty customers and the safe patch is already reviewed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It takes Michael a month of logs to see that his longest delays came after review approval, so he merges the small patch inside the maintenance window.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a failing unit test beside the release checklist

skillTargets: choose the professional response when mood, shame, or readiness tries to cancel the work appointment
distinguish routine that protects the calling from routine that becomes empty performance
analyze when an amateur posture is hiding inside sophisticated reasons
evaluate whether a proposed standard is impersonal craft discipline or self-punishing grind

tryThisNowSpec: Choose the next work appointment you are likely to renegotiate; write the first artifact-producing action on the calendar event and make that action happen before any mood check.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a research-like aside on why routine lowers daily negotiation without praising grind
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
